question: Which of the following organisms does NOT show asexual reproduction by means of fission?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Earthworm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Leishmania reproduces asexually by binary fission, where the organism divides into two equal parts.
 
• Amoeba also undergoes binary fission, a type of asexual reproduction where the cell splits into two identical daughter cells.
 
• Earthworms reproduce sexually and do not undergo asexual reproduction by means of fission.
 
• Plasmodium, the parasite responsible for malaria, reproduces asexually by multiple fission within the host's red blood cells and liver cells.
 
• Earthworms are hermaphrodites, meaning each individual possesses both male and female reproductive organs, and they reproduce through copulation and exchange of sperm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Binary Fission**

 
 
• A common method of asexual reproduction in prokaryotes and some single-celled eukaryotes.
 
• Involves the division of a single organism into two parts, each of which grows into a new organism.
 
 
 
• **Multiple Fission**
 
 
• A form of asexual reproduction where the nucleus divides multiple times before the cell splits into many new cells.
 
• Commonly seen in some protozoa and algae, like Plasmodium.
 
 
 
• **Hermaphroditism**
 
 
• A condition in which an organism has both male and female reproductive organs.
 
• Common in some invertebrates like earthworms, as well as in many plants.
